documentation_findings.finding: OpenCode exposes configurable input_paste (default Ctrl+V), input_submit (Enter), and input_newline (modified Enter or Ctrl+J) separately. Some terminals require explicit modified-Enter encoding.
Bracketed paste is a terminal protocol requested by the application using mode 2004, with distinct begin/end markers around pasted input.
Terminal-emulator paste/selection handling is separate from the application. Xfce distinguishes selected text from explicitly copied clipboard text.

bridge_recommendations_inferred_from_doc: Model terminal clipboard gesture, PTY text transport/framing, newline, submit, interrupt and exit as separate profile fields; do not equate Shift+Insert or Shift+RightClick with an application-level command.

For direct PTY mode, honor observed bracketed-paste negotiation and send the separate configured submission key only after complete input delivery; no OS clipboard gesture is required by this tested route.
A native-window backend can expose configurable OS key/mouse paste chords, including the user-mentioned Shift+Insert or Shift+RightClick, but those gestures were not tested here.
Test stable readiness, process liveness and asynchronous startup errors before dispatch; the prior Codex transient composer was insufficient.

Cover Unicode/multiline/large text, payloads containing escape or bracketed-paste marker bytes, prompt rejection and permission states, shell fallback prevention, cancellation and repeated dispatch before claiming broader compatibility.
OpenCode mini mode is an observed working profile; full-screen OpenCode TUI, other versions, other platforms, game turn acceptance and the existing bridge implementation remain unverified.
